_comment: AHEAD premixed swirl burner, reconstructed. The published mesh is an
external dataset the tutorial only links to, and the geometry is given
in the case README as prose, so this is a reconstruction from the
dimensions stated there rather than the mesh the paper used.
Taken from the README: the cylindrical mixing chamber is 34 mm across,
so rings[0] = 17 mm. Air enters it through an 8 mm axial inlet, 8 radial
slits that impose the swirl, and 12 dilution holes; fuel through 16
ports of 0.8 mm around a truncated centre body at its bottom. None of
that is resolved here: by the mixing-chamber exit the stream is premixed
at phi = 0.6, which is what the case is about, so the whole injector is
represented by its exit condition -- a swirled premixed inlet at the
bottom of the mixing tube. Resolving 8 slits, 12 holes and 16 ports
would need the CAD and snappyHexMesh, neither of which is here.
The combustion chamber radius and length are set from the case's own
system/sampleDict, whose lines run to y = +-50 mm and whose highest
